title: Inguinal hernia
subject: surgery
summary: Place the sac against the epigastric vessels, then choose the right risk, test and operation.

objectives.text: Decide whether a sac is direct or indirect from its route relative to the inferior epigastric vessels
Pick the true boundaries of Hesselbach's triangle and the exam-key inferior border, rejecting rings and Cooper's ligament
Tell inguinal from femoral hernia by position relative to the pubic tubercle
Choose congenital or acquired cause for each hernia type and predict its clinical picture and reduction
Match the deep ring occlusion test and Zieman's test to the hernia type they separate
Pick the correct 'most common' answer for hernia type, sex, age and sliding contents
Choose which hernia is most likely to strangulate, separating 'groin' from 'inguinal' wording
Pick the first step and investigation of choice in a groin lump, including strangulation and occult hernia
Choose the operation that fits the patient: child, adult open, bilateral or recurrent, tissue repair, mesh
Name the nerve at risk in open versus laparoscopic repair and the triangles of doom and pain
Match Amyand's, de Garengeot, Littre's and Richter's hernias to their contents and site

traps.trap: Direct and indirect hernias swapped relative to the inferior epigastric vessels
Deep ring, superficial ring or Cooper's ligament taken as a boundary of Hesselbach's triangle (merges TR3)
Femoral hernia taken as the most common hernia in females; inguinal hernia taken as more common in women (merges TR6)
Adult repair (mesh or herniorrhaphy) offered as the operation for a child's inguinal hernia
Direct hernia taken as the more likely to strangulate
Indirect inguinal chosen for 'groin hernia most likely to strangulate'; femoral missed
Forceful taxis attempted first in a strangulated hernia
Wrong investigation level for hernia, with CT or herniography first for occult hernia, or imaging for a clinically evident hernia (merges TR13)
Nerve injury attributed to the wrong procedure (open versus laparoscopic)
Laparoscopic repair chosen for every hernia, ignoring the primary unilateral qualifier
Bassini taken as the standard or classic open repair
Deep ring occlusion test result reversed
Zieman finger sites and invagination tip and pulp mapped to the wrong hernia
Scrotal descent and reduction direction assigned to a direct hernia
Contents and boundaries of the triangles of doom and pain swapped (merges TR26)
Conjoint tendon assigned to the anterior wall of the canal
Direct hernia treated as congenital, arising in a patent processus vaginalis; funicular and congenital types reversed (merges TR32)
Amyand's and de Garengeot's appendix hernias swapped by site
Herniotomy, herniorrhaphy and hernioplasty confused, with mesh repair called herniorrhaphy
Femoral hernia placed above and medial to the pubic tubercle

choices.label: Not sure, give me a hint

K1.text: **Inguinal hernia** is the most common type of abdominal wall hernia in both men and women.

K2.text: **Indirect** inguinal hernia is the most common type of inguinal hernia overall, in both sexes, and in children.

K3.text: An indirect hernia passes through the **deep ring, lateral** to the inferior epigastric vessels; a direct hernia bulges through **Hesselbach's triangle, medial** to them.

K4.text: **Hesselbach's triangle** is bounded by the **inferior epigastric artery** laterally, the **lateral border of the rectus sheath** (rectus abdominis) medially and the **inguinal ligament** inferiorly.

K5.text: The deep ring lies about **1.25 cm above the midinguinal point**.

K6.text: An inguinal hernia emerges **above and medial to the pubic tubercle**; a femoral hernia lies **below and lateral** to it.

K9.text: In children the operation is **herniotomy** alone (high ligation and excision of the sac), without repair of the posterior wall.

K10.text: **Laparoscopic repair (TEP/TAPP)** is preferred for **bilateral** hernias and for **recurrence after an open repair**.

K11.text: A hernia is the protrusion of a viscus or part of a viscus through an abnormal opening in the wall of the cavity that contains it.

K12.text: **Indirect (oblique)** inguinal hernia: the sac enters the inguinal canal through the deep ring, lateral to the inferior epigastric vessels, and travels along the canal within the spermatic cord coverings.

K13.text: **Direct** inguinal hernia: the sac bulges forwards through the posterior wall of the canal (transversalis fascia) in Hesselbach's triangle, medial to the inferior epigastric vessels.

K15.text: **Herniotomy** is excision of the sac; **herniorrhaphy** is herniotomy plus repair of the posterior wall with the patient's own tissue; **hernioplasty** is reinforcement of the posterior wall with a prosthetic mesh.

K18.text: **Anterior wall**: external oblique aponeurosis throughout, reinforced laterally by the internal oblique.

K19.text: **Posterior wall**: transversalis fascia throughout, reinforced medially by the **conjoint tendon**.

K25.text: An indirect hernia is congenital in origin, arising in a **patent processus vaginalis**.

K26.text: A direct hernia is acquired, from **weakness of the posterior wall** (transversalis fascia).

K27.text: Inguinal hernia is far more common in **males** than in females.

K33.text: The processus vaginalis normally obliterates after testicular descent; persistence of the whole process gives a congenital hernia reaching the testis, while partial persistence gives a funicular hernia stopping above the testis.

K35.text: A **narrow neck** at the deep ring makes indirect hernias more liable to obstruction and strangulation than direct hernias.

K36.text: **Strangulation** occurs when the blood supply of the contents is cut off: venous return is obstructed first, the contents swell, and arterial supply then fails, leading to gangrene.

K41.text: **Indirect** hernia: oblique, pear-shaped swelling that commonly descends into the scrotum and reduces upwards, laterally and backwards.

K42.text: **Direct** hernia: globular swelling near the pubic tubercle that reduces straight backwards, rarely descends into the scrotum, and is often bilateral in elderly men.

K47.text: **Strangulated** hernia: tense, tender, irreducible swelling with **no cough impulse**, often with features of intestinal obstruction and systemic toxicity.

cards.q: First step in a tense, tender, irreducible groin lump with vomiting?
cards.a: Resuscitate and take to emergency surgery; avoid forceful taxis.

cards.q: Operation of choice for a child's inguinal hernia, and why?
cards.a: Herniotomy alone, because the defect is a patent processus vaginalis with a normal posterior wall.

cards.q: Standard open repair for an adult, and the older exam key?
cards.a: Lichtenstein mesh repair; older PYQs expected Bassini.

cards.q: Nerve most at risk in open versus laparoscopic repair?
cards.a: Open: ilioinguinal. Laparoscopic: lateral femoral cutaneous.

cards.q: Triangle of doom versus triangle of pain: boundaries and contents?
cards.a: Doom: between the vas and the gonadal vessels, holds the external iliac vessels. Pain: lateral to the gonadal vessels, below the iliopubic tract, holds the nerves.

cards.q: Investigation of choice for an occult hernia?

cards.a: Sac excision; plus own-tissue wall repair; plus prosthetic mesh.

cards.q: What bounds Hesselbach's triangle, and which inferior boundary do exam keys expect?
cards.a: Inferior epigastric artery laterally, rectus sheath medially, inguinal ligament below. Exam keys use the inguinal ligament, not Cooper's ligament.

cards.q: Most common groin hernia, and most common hernia in children?
cards.a: Indirect inguinal hernia in both cases; inguinal is the commonest abdominal wall hernia.

cards.q: Which groin hernia strangulates most, and why does the neck matter?
cards.a: Femoral hernia among groin hernias. An indirect hernia's narrow neck at the deep ring makes it strangulate more than a direct one.

cards.q: Which operation for a bilateral or recurrent hernia, and which for a primary unilateral adult hernia?
cards.a: Laparoscopic TEP or TAPP for bilateral or recurrent; open Lichtenstein tension-free mesh for a primary unilateral adult hernia.

cards.q: Amyand's versus de Garengeot's versus Littre's?
cards.a: Amyand's: appendix in an inguinal sac. De Garengeot's: appendix in a femoral sac. Littre's: Meckel's diverticulum.
